checks.title: Try a new case
checks.instruction: Try these questions without opening notes or model answers first. Submit the whole set before viewing feedback. This is an optional independent practice check, not an exam or a new completion requirement.

mc.prompt: A case states that light is focused normally and photoreceptors respond, but the optic nerve cannot carry signals. Which step is directly affected?
mc.answer: Transmission of retinal information toward the brain
options: Transmission of retinal information toward the brain
Entry of light through the pupil
The ability of the cornea to bend light
The production of sound pressure waves
mc.explanation: The stated problem occurs after retinal detection. A working optical system cannot replace the neural output pathway.

mc.prompt: A plan compares two body regions for touch discrimination but also uses stronger pressure on one region. Why can it not isolate the effect of body region?
mc.answer: Both body region and contact pressure changed
options: Both body region and contact pressure changed
A responding variable must never be measured
Repeated trials always remove every confounding variable
The prediction is automatically a result
mc.explanation: More than one changed factor can explain a difference, so pressure should be controlled.

mc.prompt: In a described movement, the head turns left and then stops. Which structure may still be bent briefly by continued relative fluid movement?
options: A semicircular-canal cupula
The optic disc
The lens suspensory ligaments
A taste bud in the inner ear
mc.explanation: Canal fluid can continue moving briefly relative to the stopped canal, bending the cupula.

writing.prompt: A student says, “A brighter object and a nearer object require the same eye adjustment.” Explain why this is incomplete. Name the main adjustment for each change and trace the muscle–ligament–lens sequence for the nearer object.
writing.model: Greater brightness mainly calls for the iris to reduce pupil size and limit light entry. A nearer object calls for accommodation: the ciliary muscle contracts, ligament tension decreases, and the lens becomes rounder to bend light more strongly. The two adjustments have different jobs and can occur together.
criteria: Contraction → reduced ligament tension → rounder lens

checks.title: Try a new case
checks.instruction: Try these questions without opening notes or model answers first. Submit the whole set before viewing feedback. This is an optional independent practice check, not an exam or a new completion requirement.

mc.prompt: A case states that the anterior pituitary cannot release enough TSH, while the thyroid could respond to stimulation. Which prediction follows?
mc.answer: Thyroxine can be low because the stimulating signal is insufficient
options: Thyroxine can be low because the stimulating signal is insufficient
Thyroxine must be high because all low hormones increase TSH
The thyroid takes over production of pituitary TSH
Aldosterone must be completely absent
mc.explanation: Reduced TSH can limit thyroid output. The defect is in the stimulating signal, not necessarily the thyroid’s ability to respond.

mc.prompt: Which observation most directly distinguishes aldosterone action from ADH action?
mc.answer: Increased kidney sodium reabsorption rather than a direct increase in water permeability
options: Increased kidney sodium reabsorption rather than a direct increase in water permeability
Both can affect body fluid
Both have a hormone name
Both must be made in the posterior pituitary
mc.explanation: The immediate kidney action differs: aldosterone affects sodium/potassium handling, while ADH directly affects water permeability.

mc.prompt: A case describes high blood glucose because target tissues respond poorly to insulin, even though insulin is still present. What is the key mechanism?
mc.answer: Reduced target response to the hormone
options: Reduced target response to the hormone
Complete absence of every endocrine gland
Failure of the adrenal medulla to detect light
Glucagon becoming glycogen in the pancreas
mc.explanation: The stated problem is insulin resistance. Hormone presence alone does not guarantee a normal target response.

writing.prompt: A case states that cortisol is low because the adrenal cortex cannot respond normally, while the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary are functioning. Predict ACTH and explain the feedback. Then explain why the rapid adrenal-medulla pathway is a different route.
writing.model: Low cortisol reduces feedback inhibition of the functioning hypothalamus and pituitary, so ACTH tends to rise. The cortex defect can still prevent adequate cortisol output. The rapid pathway uses sympathetic neurons to stimulate the adrenal medulla, which releases epinephrine and norepinephrine; it does not use ACTH as its main incoming signal.
criteria: ACTH tends to rise despite low cortical output
